{!Contact.FirstName},
Thank you for your interest in the Master of Science (MS) in Communication Disorders at Arizona State University! I look forward to assisting you a you consider your options at ASU.
About the Program The MS in Communication Disorders is designed to prepare students to become certified speech-language pathologists. The MS in Communication Disorders education program in speech-language pathology is accredited by the Council on Academic Accreditation in Audiology and Speech-Language pathology (CAA) of the American Speech-Language-Hearing Association.
The Speech and Hearing Clinic located on the Tempe campus provides the campus-based clinical training for the Communication Disorders program. The department has established affiliations with a wide variety of community partners for clinical rotation opportunities for our graduate students, including community preschool, hospital, private practice and public schools.
About Admissions Please visit our applying to the Communication Disorders, MS site at chs.asu.edu/shs/applying-communication-disorders-ms-program and be sure to review our FAQs page at chs.asu.edu/shs/frequently-asked-questions. Here you will find more information about the application process.
We accept applications for fall only with a deadline of January 15.
You can estimate the cost of your attendance based on current tuition and fees by visiting this site: students.asu.edu/tuitionandfees and using our tuition calculator.
Thank you for your interest in the MS in Communication Disorders program at Arizona State University. Please let me know if you have any questions.
Kindest regards, Anita Youmara Graduate Program Coordinator Department of Speech and Hearing Science College of Health Solutions 975 S. Myrtle Avenue | Tempe, AZ 85287 | MC 0102
